encoding: standalone/<id>.bin uses the Slice 2B case encoding: the concatenation of the tensors x, w, scales, biases (little-endian; U32/F32 4-byte words, BF16 2-byte words) at the recorded offsets; w/scales/biases are the ORACLE's expected plane bytes, never sliced from a shard
files_listing_method: inside fixtures/native-composition: find checkpoints mutations standalone -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs shasum -a 256 | shasum -a 256

ck-a-single.source_identity_method: inside the checkpoint directory: LC_ALL=C shasum -a 256 *.safetensors | shasum -a 256

ck-a-sibling.source_identity_method: inside the checkpoint directory: LC_ALL=C shasum -a 256 *.safetensors | shasum -a 256

ck-b-sharded.source_identity_method: inside the checkpoint directory: LC_ALL=C shasum -a 256 *.safetensors | shasum -a 256

cases.note: first expert; vector x; default 4-bit; single shard; tensor at a nonzero data offset
last expert; matrix x (M_eff 32: matrix family on every architecture)
middle expert of a second module with identical geometry and a different placement
middle expert; vector x
8-bit resolved by explicit per-module override over a 4-bit default; first expert; matrix x
8-bit override; last expert; vector x
4-bit by default inside the mixed checkpoint; last of two experts; K 512 (qmv_fast)
first expert whose scales range starts at the first byte of its shard's data section
8-bit override; weight, scales and biases in three different shards; middle expert; N 128
last expert, companions in three shards; K 128 (qmv_quad); biases end at their shard's end
admitted expert of the module whose expert 1 is refused (inh-meta-range-e1): refusal is per plane
A-B-A step 0: 8-bit override module, expert 1
A-B-A step 1: a different module at a different bit width (4-bit default) in the same child
A-B-A step 2: the step-0 selection and x again; A output must equal step 0's bit for bit
expert index E (4 of 4 experts): one past the last expert
expert index 2^64-1: must be refused as out of range, never wrapped or narrowed
empty index path for a tensor with one leading dimension
two indices for a tensor with one leading dimension

range-resolution probe: begin 2^64-8, len 16 over a valid backing; begin + len overflows u64. Unreachable through an admitted catalog and a validated triple (catalog rules 10-12, Slice 1 C-SLICE); this probes the composition layer's own checked range arithmetic directly
the backing for the biases' shard is a window one byte shorter than the shard; the selected biases plane ends at the shard's last byte (a valid file, an insufficient backing)
triple resolved from ck-a-single, backing loaded from ck-a-sibling: identical headers and catalog, different payload; only the payload-inclusive source identity distinguishes them
a triple built through the public AffineTriple::new for module block.0.stack_a from stack_a's weight and stack_b's scales and biases (identical shapes, so Slice 1 admits it)
the selected plane has N = 32 (N % 64 != 0): Slice 2B D-GEOM refuses it after a correct selection
expert 1 carries one normal bfloat16 scale 2^-33 < 2^-32; experts 0 and 2 are admitted
x last dimension 128 against the plane's logical K = 256 (derived from the resolved spec, not from the packed width)
selection arithmetic uses expert 2 while the plane identity records expert 1
weight plane stride one u32 word too large (expert 2 of 4, so the range stays inside the tensor); a stride error is invisible on expert 0 by construction
weight and biases of expert 3, scales of expert 2
weight and scales of expert 1, biases of expert 0 (companions in three shards)
the 8-bit override is dropped from the configuration; Slice 1 resolution refuses (InconsistentOverride, implied bits 8) before any selection
the plane records the 4-bit default instead of the resolved 8-bit override; ranges and bytes are unchanged, so only the identity comparison detects it (the bridge's R-META would refuse later)
